title: National AI in Work Day and how to use AI tools at your job
dek: September 30 is National AI in Work Day, a good time to think about how to use AI tools at work in a way that actually helps.
body: For those of you starting an early shift, today is National AI in Work Day. It focuses on using AI responsibly in the workplace to help people do their jobs well, and it arrives at a time when a lot of us are figuring that out as we go.

For many people, AI tools are most helpful with the small, repetitive tasks. They can summarize a long document, draft a first version of a routine email, or organize notes after a meeting. That leaves more time for the parts of the job that need full attention. EveryHour itself is written with AI, and the site says so on every post.

It also pays to be careful. Read everything before you send it, check facts yourself, and do not paste private information into a tool unless your workplace has said it is allowed. When something important is on the line, your own judgment should stay in charge.

I think the best approach is to treat these tools like a helpful new coworker. They are fast and eager, but they still need clear instructions and someone to review their work. Being honest with your team about when you used them helps build trust too.
Today, try using an AI tool for one small task you usually dread, then review the result closely. You will learn quickly where it saves you time and where you still need to do it yourself.
